{{Short description|American basketball player (born 2000)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2024}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Seth Lundy | image = Seth Lundy.jpg | image_size = | caption = Lundy with [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] in 2021 | position = [[Shooting guard]] / [[small forward]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 4 | weight_lb = 220 | league = | team = Free agent | number = | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2000|4|2}} | birth_place = [[Paulsboro, New Jersey]], U.S. | high_school = [[Roman Catholic High School|Roman Catholic]]
([[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]) | college = [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] (2019–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 46 | draft_team = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|full=y}} | team1 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team2 = →[[College Park Skyhawks]] | highlights = }} '''Seth Xavier Lundy''' (born April 2, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[College Park Skyhawks]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State Nittany Lions]]. ==Early life and high school career== Lundy grew up in [[Paulsboro, New Jersey]] and attended [[Roman Catholic High School]] in [[Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania.{{cite web |last=Carino |first=Jerry |date=March 14, 2023 |title=March Madness: Top 10 New Jerseyans to watch in the NCAA Tournament, ranked |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2023/03/14/march-madness-top-12-new-jerseyans-to-watch-in-the-ncaa-tournament/70003303007/ |access-date=June 5, 2023 |work=[[Asbury Park Press]]}} He averaged 16.4 points and 8.7 rebounds per game as a junior.{{cite web |last=Gallen |first=Daniel |date=April 26, 2018 |title=Roman Catholic basketball star Seth Lundy picks up SEC offer |url=https://www.pennlive.com/highschoolsports/article/roman-catholic-basketball-star-seth-lundy-picks-up-sec-offer/ |access-date=June 5, 2023 |work=[[The Patriot-News]]}} Lundy committed to playing college basketball for [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] over offers from [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] and [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]].{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/high_school/pennsylvania/seth-lundy-penn-state-basketball-commitment-recruiting-roman-catholic-high-school-20181005.html|title=Seth Lundy joins Roman Catholic basketball pipeline to Penn State|first=Rick|last=O'Brien|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=October 5, 2018|access-date=June 5, 2023}} ==College career== Lundy averaged 5.3 points per game during his freshman season at Penn State.{{cite web |last=Hayes |first=Elton |date=March 22, 2023 |title=Lundy to declare for NBA Draft; Pair enters transfer portal |url=https://www.dailyitem.com/sports/lundy-to-declare-for-nba-draft-pair-enters-transfer-portal/article_57e2b56a-c915-11ed-ad34-4f77ffe5da08.html |access-date=June 5, 2023 |work=[[The Daily Item (Sunbury)|The Daily Item]]}} He averaged 10.1 points and 4.2 rebounds over 25 games with 15 starts as a sophomore. After the season Lundy entered the [[NCAA]] transfer portal, but ultimately withdrew and returned to Penn State.{{cite web |last=Gallen |first=Daniel |date=April 15, 2021 |title=Penn State men’s basketball forward Seth Lundy leaves transfer portal: report |url=https://www.pennlive.com/pennstatefootball/2021/04/penn-state-mens-basketball-forward-seth-lundy-leaves-transfer-portal-report.html |access-date=June 5, 2023 |work=[[The Patriot-News]]}} He started all 30 of the Nittany Lions' games during his junior season and averaged 11.9 points and 4.9 rebounds while leading the team with 20 total [[blocked shots]].{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-jalen-pickett-seth-lundy-micah-shrewsberry-college-basketball-4298930472ad4897f5da4788fc9955ad|title=Shrewsberry hopes Penn State takes a step forward in Year 2|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=October 19, 2022|access-date=June 5, 2023}} Lundy was named honorable mention All-[[Big Ten Conference]] as a senior after averaging 14.2 points and 6.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://nittanylionswire.usatoday.com/2023/05/02/jalen-pickett-and-seth-lundy-invited-to-nba-combine/|title=Jalen Pickett and Seth Lundy invited to NBA combine|first=Kevin|last=McGuire|website=Nittany Lions Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=May 2, 2023|access-date=June 5, 2023}} After the season, he declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Gabriel |first=Kerith |date=March 22, 2023 |title=Penn State and former Roman guard Seth Lundy declaring for NBA Draft |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/penn-state/seth-lundy-nba-draft-penn-state-ncaa-mens-basketball-20230322.html |access-date=June 5, 2023 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]}} ==Professional career== Lundy was selected in the second round of the 2023 NBA draft by the [[Atlanta Hawks]], with the 46th overall pick.{{cite news|first=Isabella|last=DiAmore|title=Penn State’s Seth Lundy drafted by the Atlanta Hawks in the second round|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/penn-state/seth-lundy-penn-state-roman-catholic-atlanta-hawks-nba-draft-20230623.html|work=Philadelphia Inquirer|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}} Lundy and [[Jalen Pickett]] were the first two Nittany Lions teammates to be selected in the same NBA draft.{{cite news|first=Jerry|last=DiPaola|title=Penn State pair Jalen Pickett, Seth Lundy picked in 2nd round of NBA Draft by Nuggets, Hawks|url=https://triblive.com/sports/penn-state-pair-jalen-pickett-seth-lundy-picked-in-2nd-round-of-nba-draft-by-nuggets-hawks/|work=Pittsburgh Tribune Review|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}}{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Hymowitz|title=Jalen Pickett, Seth Lundy chosen in NBA Draft in historic night for Penn State basketball|url=https://www.centredaily.com/sports/college/penn-state-university/psu-basketball/article276634101.html|work=Centre Daily Times|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}} On July 6, 2023, Lundy signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite news |last=Windhorst |first=Brian |author-link=Brian Windhorst |date=July 6, 2023 |title=Dejounte Murray, Hawks finalizing 4-year, $112 million extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37971383 |access-date=July 6, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |quote=The Hawks also signed second-round draft choice Seth Lundy and undrafted free agent Miles Norris to two-way contracts.}} On December 15, he made his NBA debut in a 125–104 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]], scoring two points in the game. On May 14, 2024, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] announced that Lundy had undergone surgery on May 1 to remove a medial ankle [[bone spur]] on his left ankle.{{cite tweet|author=Atlanta Hawks|title=An @emoryhealthcare injury update: Seth Lundy underwent left ankle surgery on May 1 to remove a medial ankle bone spur. The surgery was performed by Dr. Richard Ferkel at the Southern California Orthopedic Institute. Lundy will miss the NBA2K Summer League and is expected to make a full recovery prior to the 2024-25 season.|number=1790431336097825151|date=May 14, 2024|user=ATLHawks|access-date=May 14, 2024}} On July 9, 2024, Lundy signed another two-way contract with the Hawks,{{cite news|title=Hawks Sign Seth Lundy to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-seth-lundy-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2024|access-date=July 18, 2024}} but was waived on December 18.{{cite news|title=Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers on Seth Lundy|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-on-seth-lundy|website=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2024|access-date=December 18, 2024}} According to [[Shams Charania]], the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] waived center [[Kai Jones]] to clear space for Lundy to sign a [[two-way contract]] with the team on March 1, 2025.{{Cite web |last=Caudell |first=Jackson |date=2025-03-01 |title=Former Atlanta Hawks 2nd Round Pick Signs Two-Way Contract With The Los Angeles Clippers |url=https://www.si.com/nba/hawks/news/former-atlanta-hawks-2nd-round-pick-signs-two-way-contract-with-the-los-angeles-clippers-01jn9v2wdpk8 |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=SI.com |language=en-US}} On July 9, Lundy was waived by the Clippers.{{Cite web |last=Stinar |first=Ben |date=2025-07-15 |title=LA Clippers Release 1-Year NBA Player |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/la-clippers-release-1-year-nba-player-seth-lundy |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=SI.com |language=en-US }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026
